brand.name: Promise
locale.label: Language
hero.title: Every gift is a promise to give back.
hero.lead: Promise puts the wedding envelope on NEAR. The invitation is a soulbound NFT that holds the money until the event. Afterwards the contract remembers who owes whom.
hero.caption: Drawing of the four states of one card. In the demo, the card is drawn by the contract itself.
problem.title: The record lives in a paper book.
problem.p1: In Indonesia and much of Asia, an envelope at a wedding is a debt of honor, not a present. If someone gave 100 at your wedding, you are expected to give 100 or more at theirs. Everyone knows this.
problem.p2: The record sits in a guest book that gets lost, swapped, or argued over by relatives twenty years later.
problem.p3: Digital angpao apps send money. They do not remember what you owe.
states.title: One card, four states.
states.lead: Every guest holds a soulbound invitation. It cannot be sold or moved. What it shows depends only on what the contract holds.
states.invited.title: Invited
states.invited.body: The host invites you by account, or you RSVP from a shared link. The card is empty.
states.sealed.title: Sealed
states.sealed.body: You lock tUSDC inside the invitation in one transaction. The amount stays hidden until the event.
states.opened.title: Opened
states.opened.body: On the day, the host checks you in. The money moves to the host and the card shows what you gave.
states.repaid.title: Repaid
states.repaid.body: When the host later gives at your event, the contract settles the oldest claim first and this card flips.
states.refund: If the host cancels, every sealed envelope goes back to its owner, whoever presses the button.
ledger.title: The contract keeps the guest book.
ledger.lead: When an envelope opens, the host owes the guest that amount. When the host later gives at the guest's event, the contract repays the oldest claim first. Anything above the debt becomes a new claim in the other direction.
ledger.caption: Example from the contract spec, amounts in tUSDC. Ayu hosts first, then goes to Budi's event.
ledger.row1.event: Budi gives 5 at Ayu's wedding. Ayu opens it.
ledger.row2.event: Citra gives 2 at the same wedding.
ledger.row3.result: Budi's first card flips to Repaid. Ayu's new card reads Reply. The debt to Budi is 0.
ledger.row4.result: Budi's card is Repaid and Budi now owes Ayu 3.
ledger.row5.result: Ayu still owes Budi 2. Budi's card shows partly repaid.
ledger.footnote: One opening repays at most 10 older claims. Repayment cannot be forced: this is a record nobody can edit alone, not a court order.
limits.title: Limits, stated plainly.
limits.1: Repayment is social, not enforced. The value is a record nobody can edit alone.
limits.2: Amounts are public on chain. A privacy layer is on the roadmap, not built.
limits.3: Testnet only. The money is test tUSDC from our own faucet. Nothing here touches real funds.
limits.4: One contract holds every balance. Invitations are not sub-accounts.
limits.5: Crypto is not legal tender in Indonesia, so Promise is framed as a gift tradition, not a payment method.
cta.title: Run the whole story in five minutes.
cta.body: No wallet needed. Demo mode signs with test accounts whose keys are published on purpose.
footer.line: Built solo at NEAR HACKATHON 2026 by Imanuel. Testnet only, no real funds.
demo.title: Demo accounts
demo.lead: Five testnet accounts controlled by the author. Their keys are public on purpose and hold only test tokens. They exist to show every state of the card. They are not real users.
demo.walkthrough.title: The seven-step story
demo.walkthrough.lead: Switch accounts as you go. Each step shows what the card and the ledger should say.
demo.step.1: Ayu opens her hajat "Pernikahan Ayu & Bima". Three invitations: Budi, Citra, Dewi. Dewi has not sealed yet.
demo.step.2: Dewi opens her invitation and seals 5 tUSDC with a short note. The card goes from Invited to Sealed and the amount stays hidden.
demo.step.3: Ayu checks Dewi in. The card turns Opened and shows 5.00. Ayu's balance rises by 5.
demo.step.4: Ayu opens the ledger: she owes Dewi 5.00, Budi 5.00 and Citra 2.00.
demo.step.5: Budi opens his hajat "Syukuran khitanan Raka". Ayu and Citra are invited as guests.
demo.step.6: Ayu opens Budi's invitation and presses "Pay back what I owe". The suggested amount is 5.00, taken from the ledger.
demo.step.7: Budi checks Ayu in. Ayu's debt to Budi is 0 and Budi's first card now reads Repaid.
